cases.body:

cases.title: Fix `no-duplicate-selectors` false negatives for matching escaped selectors
cases.body:
## Summary

Fixes #3972

The `no-duplicate-selectors` rule now correctly detects duplicate class selectors that use different CSS escape sequence formats. For example, `.u-m\00002b` and `.u-m\+` are now recognized as duplicates since both represent `.u-m+`.

## Changes

- Added `normalizeNodeEscaping()` helper in `normalizeSelector.mjs` that uses postcss-selector-parser's getter/setter behavior to normalize CSS escaping
- Added test cases for escaped selector duplicates

## How it works

The fix leverages postcss-selector-parser's built-in value getter/setter behavior for ClassName nodes. The getter returns the unescaped value, while the setter re-escapes it in a normalized form. By doing `node.value = node.value`, we trigger this normalization, ensuring equivalent selectors compare as equal regardless of their original escape format.

Reference: https://github.com/postcss/postcss-selector-parser/blob/1b1e9c3bc10ccc3bc5f07a987caa7f2684c0b52f/src/selectors/className.js#L13-L28

cases.title: Add OCI friendly S3 chunked encoding toggle
cases.body:
Closes #11441

### Adds OCI-Friendly Chunked Encoding Toggle for Nessie Catalog S3 Clients
This PR makes the catalog’s S3 client behavior configurable so deployments targeting Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (and other S3-compatible services that reject chunked payload signatures) can disable chunked transfer encoding end-to-end. The option is exposed at the configuration API level, propagated through the catalog implementation, documented in Helm, and covered by tests.

**Key changes:**

- Introduces chunked-encoding-enabled on S3BucketOptions, plus helpers, and wires it into S3ClientSupplier so per-bucket overrides reach the AWS SDK S3Configuration.

- Extends the Helm chart (values.yaml, README, helpers, templates) and Quarkus sample config so both global defaults and per-bucket settings can toggle chunked encoding.

- Adds unit coverage (TestS3ClientSupplier) verifying default AWS behavior and explicit true/false values, preventing regressions.

- Updates the changelog to highlight the new configuration hook.

**Testing:**

`./gradlew :nessie-catalog-files-impl:test --tests org.projectnessie.catalog.files.s3.TestS3ClientSupplier`

cases.title: feat: deprecate falcon.testing.redirected in favor of contextlib
cases.body:
# Summary of Changes

Deprecates `falcon.testing.redirected` in favor of the standard library's `contextlib.redirect_stdout` and `contextlib.redirect_stderr`.

**Changes:**
- Added deprecation warning to `falcon.testing.redirected` using `falcon.util.deprecated`
- Updated internal test file (`test_cmd_inspect_app.py`) to use `contextlib` alternatives
- Scheduled for removal in Falcon 5.0

**Rationale:**
- The popular pytest framework already captures and suppresses output from successful tests by default
- The stdlib provides equivalent functionality via `contextlib.redirect_stdout` and `contextlib.redirect_stderr`
- Reduces maintenance burden by removing redundant utility

# Related Issues

Fixes #2569

cases.title: Fix Whisper tokenizer to use extra_special_tokens for Transformers v5 compatibility
cases.body:
## What did you change?

Updated the Whisper tokenizer logic to use `extra_special_tokens` instead of `additional_special_tokens` when reading/adding special tokens.

---

## Why did you make this change?

Transformers v5 removed `tokenization_utils_fast.py` and unified the tokenizer APIs. espnet/whisper still depended on older GPT2Tokenizer attributes (`additional_special_tokens`), which caused errors with the new API. Switching to `extra_special_tokens` fixes compatibility with v5.

---

## Is your PR small enough?

yes. 2 files, 4 add/deletions

---

## Additional Context

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/MIGRATION_GUIDE_V5.md

cases.title: feat: add generate_strategy option to litgpt serve
cases.body:
## What does this PR do?
This PR adds a `generate_strategy` option to the `litgpt serve` command. This allows users to explicitly specify the generation strategy (e.g., `"sequential"`, `"tensor_parallel"`) when initializing the model for serving.

## Motivation
Previously, the `generate_strategy` was hardcoded to `"sequential"` in `serve.py` when verifying `devices > 1`, giving users no option to choose alternative strategies like `"tensor_parallel"` which might be preferred for certain deployments.

## Who can review this?
@bhimrazy 
Anyone from the community is free to review once the tests are passed.
